_note: Inputs of dc_sim.dc_design (architecture v2: pooled GPU nodes, CPU sandbox pool, context-memory pool, shared QPU service, agents PARK their session while a QPU sub-task runs). Shared sections (case_b, cpu, economics, quantum, pod) are read from arch_study.json. EVERYTHING here is an ASSUMPTION unless it says FROM quantum_arch / FROM dc_sim assumptions. The class mix and the quantum-eligible call densities are the scenario, not data: nobody has measured them.

coding_agents.note: case B (slides). Calls: a solver/optimiser tool that happens to be quantum-backed; rare.

mechanical.note: mechanical engineers: optimisation sub-problems (small, classical is cheap)

finance.note: financial engineers: large linear-algebra sub-problems (quantum_arch states no advantage for this kernel)

classical_fallback_module_hours.note: FROM dc_sim assumptions classical_fallback_defaults (ASSUMPTIONS there): cost of the best classical method at the same accuracy.

classical_max_note: A call that would cost more than this classically is NOT SERVED by the GPU-only reference (about 64 modules for 3 hours). On a QPU it is served. Unserved calls are valued at this cap in the sizing objective. ASSUMPTION.
induced_note: Assumption 1 of the user: with QPUs available, more QPU tasks get created. The call densities above are multiplied by this factor in a scenario; the GPU-only reference faces the same calls (and cannot serve the expensive ones).

parking.note: Park: the session context moves to the context-memory pool; on resume it is copied back (transfer_gbps) or, for recompute_share of the resumes, re-prefilled (cached_ctx_tokens). Hold: the session keeps its KV cache in GPU HBM (ctx_gb of hbm_gb_per_module) for the whole wait + run. Capacity, share and token numbers are ASSUMPTIONS; pool power and capex FROM dc_sim assumptions (ctxmem_pool).

classical_cost_scale_note: Multiplies every classical fallback cost; used for sensitivities (the fallback costs are the least certain input).
